topics.summary: The POS system experiences frequent outages during peak hours, causing cashiers to lose internet access and resulting in lost revenue for the company.
topics.raw_quote: when the WAN drops, our POS goes fully offline — can't even process a cash sale because it can't validate the SKU pricing locally.

topics.summary: The mobile app search feature often returns out-of-stock items, leading to a negative customer experience and NPS scores.
topics.raw_quote: NPS for customers who hit this is -30. Customers who don't hit it are +18.

topics.summary: The pharmacy refill process is confusing due to the use of two separate systems, leading to issues with medication availability and customer satisfaction.
topics.raw_quote: It's because we have TWO refill flows: the in-app one, and the IVR phone line. They write to different systems and the systems don't reconcile in real time.
topics.speaker: Anika

topics.summary: Customers are unsure about how they earn or lose loyalty tier status, leading to frustration and confusion.
topics.raw_quote: The downgrade timing isn't clear from any customer-facing surface.
topics.speaker: Priya

topics.summary: The store-associate handheld scanners are outdated and lack modern features, causing issues with inventory management and customer satisfaction.

stories.title: Enable offline cash sales with local SKU pricing validation
stories.description: The current POS system cannot process cash sales when the WAN is down because it cannot validate SKU pricing locally. This story aims to enable local SKU pricing validation to allow cash sales to proceed offline.
stories.user_story: As a store associate, I want to process cash sales even when the store's internet connection is down, so that we can avoid lost revenue and serve customers without interruption.
acceptance_criteria: Given the store's WAN connection is down, when a store associate attempts a cash sale, then the POS system processes the sale.
Given the store's WAN connection is down, when a store associate attempts a cash sale, then the system validates SKU pricing using local data.
Given the WAN connection is restored after offline cash sales, when the POS reconnects, then all offline cash transactions are synchronized with central systems.
stories.priority_rationale: Frequent POS outages during peak hours lead to cashiers losing internet access, directly causing lost revenue for the company, as stated by Hiroshi.

evidence.raw_quote: when the WAN drops, our POS goes fully offline — can't even process a cash sale because it can't validate the SKU pricing locally.
evidence.speaker: Hiroshi

stories.title: Upgrade store associate handheld inventory scanners to a modern, secure platform
stories.description: The current store-associate handheld inventory scanners run on an outdated operating system (Android 7) that can no longer receive security patches.
stories.user_story: As a store associate, I want to use modern, secure handheld scanners, so that I can efficiently manage inventory and serve customers without security risks or operational limitations.
acceptance_criteria: Given a store associate uses the new handheld scanner, when they perform inventory tasks, then the device operates on a supported and patched operating system.
Given a store associate uses the new handheld scanner, when they access inventory data, then the device provides modern features for efficient management.
Given the new handheld scanners are deployed, when a security scan is performed on the devices, then no critical or high-severity vulnerabilities related to an outdated OS are found.
Given a store associate needs to look up customer information via the handheld, when the feature is used, then all customer identity interactions adhere to NSID federation requirements.
stories.priority_rationale: The current scanners run on an unpatched Android 7, posing a significant security risk and impacting store operations and customer satisfaction.

evidence.raw_quote: The store-side handheld inventory scanners are running Android 7. They can't get security patches anymore.
evidence.speaker: Hiroshi
